steps.text: Do not diagnose mesenteric adenitis in a child who is **toxic**, has **localised peritonism**, or is getting worse. Treat that as appendicitis until proven otherwise.

glossary.mesenteric adenitis: Inflammation of the lymph nodes in the mesentery, usually causing right lower abdominal pain after an infection.
glossary.mesentery: The fold of tissue that attaches the bowel to the back of the abdomen and carries its vessels and lymph nodes.
glossary.mesenteric lymph nodes: Lymph nodes in the mesentery that drain the bowel.
glossary.reactive lymphoid hyperplasia: Enlargement of lymph nodes as they respond to infection, without being primarily infected.
glossary.terminal ileum: The last part of the small bowel, joining the caecum in the right lower abdomen; rich in lymphoid tissue.
glossary.Peyer's patches: Clusters of lymphoid tissue in the wall of the ileum.
glossary.Yersinia enterocolitica: A Gram-negative bacterium spread by contaminated food that can cause mesenteric adenitis and 'pseudoappendicitis'.
glossary.Yersinia: A genus of Gram-negative bacteria; Yersinia enterocolitica is the classic trigger of mesenteric adenitis.
glossary.Campylobacter: A common bacterial cause of gastroenteritis, often from undercooked poultry.
glossary.Salmonella: A bacterium causing food poisoning, often from eggs or poultry.
glossary.pseudoappendicitis: Illness that mimics appendicitis, classically from Yersinia mesenteric adenitis.
glossary.appendicitis: Inflammation of the appendix; the main condition mesenteric adenitis mimics.
glossary.RIF: Right iliac fossa: the right lower part of the abdomen.
glossary.right lower quadrant: The right lower quarter of the abdomen, overlapping the RIF.
glossary.URTI: Upper respiratory tract infection, such as a cold or sore throat.
glossary.gastroenteritis: Infection of the gut causing diarrhoea and vomiting.
glossary.peritonism: Signs of peritoneal irritation: guarding, rigidity, rebound and pain on movement.
glossary.guarding: Involuntary tensing of the abdominal muscles when a tender area is pressed.
glossary.rebound tenderness: Pain on sudden release of pressure on the abdomen; a sign of peritonitis.
glossary.anorexia: Loss of appetite; common in appendicitis but not in mesenteric adenitis.
glossary.low-grade fever: A mildly raised temperature, roughly 37.5 to 38.3°C.
glossary.self-limiting: Gets better on its own without treatment.
glossary.diagnosis of exclusion: A diagnosis made only once other likely causes have been ruled out.
glossary.safety-netting: Telling patients or parents which symptoms mean they should seek help again, and how.
glossary.cervical lymph nodes: Lymph nodes in the neck; often enlarged after a sore throat.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein: a blood marker that rises with inflammation or infection.
glossary.WCC: White cell count; raised in infection and inflammation.
glossary.free fluid: Fluid seen in the abdomen on imaging; a small amount can be normal or reactive.
